title: Key provenance claims and SIEM enrichment playbook
content:
Purpose
This playbook defines how Redwood captures key provenance assertions, transforms KMS/HSM events into a structured audit schema, and enriches SIEM telemetry for forensics and automated evidence bundles. It is intended for security engineers, compliance owners, and SREs who operate KMS/HSM/BYOK flows.

Scope and goals
- Ensure each key lifecycle event contains a minimal provenance claim set that supports non-repudiation and regulatory audit queries.
- Provide a canonical audit log schema for KMS and HSM activity that is SIEM-friendly and small enough to stream at scale.
- Define evidence-automation patterns: triggers, artifacts, retention, cryptographic attestation and export paths into SIEM and archive.
- Describe fallback behavior (HSM offline, software-wrapped key) and how that is signaled to downstream monitoring and compliance.

Design principles
- Immutable event records: every event emitted MUST include a cryptographic digest and correlation IDs so evidence bundles can be verified after archival.
- Redact where required: key material or secrets MUST never appear in logs; provide fingerprints and metadata instead.
- Minimal but sufficient fields: keep per-event size small to avoid high egress while preserving forensic value.
- Deterministic enrichment: SIEM enrichment must be reproducible from stored provenance and configuration.

Canonical audit event schema (flat fields, required/optional)
Each emitted audit record for KMS/HSM/BYOK operations will include the following fields. These map directly to our SIEM ingestion fields. Fields marked REQUIRED must be present.
- event_timestamp: REQUIRED, ISO8601 UTC
- event_id: REQUIRED, UUIDv4
- correlation_id: OPTIONAL, UUID used to tie multi-step ops (eg import->wrap->publish)
- trace_id: OPTIONAL, distributed-trace id for request path
- actor_type: REQUIRED, e.g., user | service | system | external-customer
- actor_id: REQUIRED, principal id (opaque)
- auth_method: REQUIRED, e.g., api_key | oauth | mTLS | hsm-attestation
- source_ip: OPTIONAL
- action: REQUIRED, short verb: key.create | key.import | key.rotate | key.activate | key.deactivate | key.delete | key.use | key.export-request | kms-policy-change | hsm-fallback | key-escrow
- outcome: REQUIRED, success | failure | partial
- resource_type: REQUIRED, e.g., tenant-key | keystore | hsm-session | wrapping-key
- resource_id: REQUIRED, opaque id
- tenant_id: REQUIRED for multi-tenant contexts
- key_fingerprint: REQUIRED for any operation touching key material (SHA256 hex of public-wrapped-key or key handle)
- key_algorithm: OPTIONAL, e.g., RSA-3072 | AES-256-GCM | ECDSA-P-256
- operation_details: OPTIONAL, short free-text (avoid PII and key bytes)
- prev_state: OPTIONAL, small token representing previous lifecycle state
- new_state: OPTIONAL
- retention_tier: OPTIONAL, e.g., audit-short | audit-long | legal-archive
- evidence_bundle_id: OPTIONAL, id of stored evidence package (if created)
- signature: OPTIONAL, base64 of signingKey(signature(event_id || timestamp || resource_id))
- request_id: OPTIONAL, proxied request id from caller
- severity: OPTIONAL, low | medium | high (used for SIEM alerting)
- tags: OPTIONAL, comma-separated short tags

Schema notes and examples
- key_fingerprint is the single canonical reference to actual key material. Example fingerprint: sha256:3f9c...
- signature field is used for evidence bundles: key-ops service signs a compact canonical string so archived bundles can be validated later.
- action values are intentionally conservative; extenders should map new verbs to these categories rather than adding many ad-hoc actions.

SIEM enrichment mapping (Elastic / Splunk friendly)
We adopt a two-stage enrichment: 1) Lightweight mapping at ingestion and 2) Deterministic enrichment by the evidence service (post-ingest). Field mapping suggestions:
- ECS/Elastic mapping:
  - @timestamp -> event_timestamp
  - event.id -> event_id
  - trace.id -> trace_id
  - user.id -> actor_id
  - user.agent -> auth_method
  - source.ip -> source_ip
  - agent.action -> action
  - event.outcome -> outcome
  - network.transport -> resource_type (custom)
  - tls.fingerprint -> key_fingerprint (custom)
  - observability.evidence.id -> evidence_bundle_id (custom)
- Splunk recommended fields (indexed):
  - _time -> event_timestamp
  - event_id
  - actor_id
  - action
  - outcome
  - tenant_id
  - key_fingerprint
  - evidence_bundle_id

Enrichment patterns
- On ingest, SIEM will create a lightweight alertable event for any hsm-fallback or key-export-request with severity >= medium.
- Evidence service will listen to correlation_id groups and create a signed evidence bundle when a complete lifecycle (import->wrap->publish) completes or when a policy threshold is hit (e.g., key material crosses regions).
- Enrichment payload includes: canonical audit slice, compressed operation log, manifest with digests, attestation certificate chain (HSM attestation if available), and a signed envelope metadata file. SIEM stores the manifest fields and link to the archive bucket.

Evidence automation flows
Trigger conditions for generating an evidence bundle:
- Any BYOK import (always generate an evidence bundle).
- Any key export or key-escrow event.
- HSM fallback or HSM-attestation-failure.
- Scheduled periodic snapshots for keys in legal-archive tier (daily/weekly depending on retention policy).
- Ad-hoc: security ops can trigger bundle creation via an API.

Evidence bundle contents (minimally):
- manifest.json (list of events with digests; small, human readable)
- operation_log.ndjson (raw canonical events used to construct manifest)
- attestation.pem (HSM attestation cert chain or software signing cert)
- proof.sig (signature over manifest by signing key)
- storage_metadata.txt (bucket/path, retention label)
- verify_instructions.md (how to validate signature and digests)

Storage and retention
- audit-short: 90 days in hot SIEM index.
- audit-long: 2 years in cold storage and evidence service index.
- legal-archive: 7+ years immutable object store (WORM) with retention labels and eDiscovery access patterns.
- Evidence bundles are written to an encrypted archive bucket managed by the evidence service and indexed in the SIEM by evidence_bundle_id.

BYOK onboarding and provenance checks (operational checklist)
1) Intake: customer submits import request with metadata, import-token, and origin claim.
2) Preflight validation: verify algorithm/length policy, determine if key can be imported into HSM or must be software-wrapped.
3) Attestation request: request HSM attestation of imported key (if HSM import). Record attestation cert chain in evidence bundle.
4) Fingerprint calculation: compute key_fingerprint (canonical SHA256 of wrapped key blob) and store in audit record.
5) Escrow policy: if customer opts for escrow, create escrow record and store in secure escrow keystore with dual-control logging.
6) Finalize: set key state to active and emit key.import event with evidence_bundle_id referencing stored attestation and manifest.

Operational knobs and SLOs for rotation and emergency rotation
- Scheduled rotation window: default 30–90 days depending on key tier. Rotation means create new key, rewrap active data keys, update metadata and roll traffic.
- Dual-write period: during rotation we may maintain both previous_key_fingerprint and new_key_fingerprint for 24–72 hours to allow in-flight operations to succeed.
- Rollback SLO: if rotation fails we must revert to prior key within 15 minutes for production-critical keys.
- Emergency rotation: generate an emergency rotation event, emit hsm-fallback if HSM unavailable, raise severity=high and notify on-call. SIEM should open an incident automatically when emergency rotation is observed.

HSM fallback and software-wrapped fallback pattern
- Detect HSM outage via health pings. On first detection, emit hsm-fallback event with severity=medium and sampling=100%.
- Create ephemeral wrapping key (ephemeral-broker) in software with a tight TTL and mark resource_type=wrapping-key with tag fallback=software.
- All subsequent key.use events MUST include fallback_reason and fallback_ttl.
- Evidence service will create a fallback evidence bundle that includes the HSM health timeline, operator actions, and wrapping-key fingerprint.
- After HSM recovery, perform an integrity check: verify no unauthorized export occurred and rotate the ephemeral wrapping key.

Sampling and noise reduction
- We adopt sampling for low-severity key.use events for quiet tenants: default 1% sampling for high-frequency ops, but 100% for admin-level operations (create/import/rotate/export).
- SIEM enrichment will surface sampled vs unsampled via field sample_rate so downstream analytics can scale metrics appropriately.

Privacy and redaction guidance
- NEVER log raw key material or private key parameters. Use key_fingerprint and algorithm fields instead.
- Request-level user context may include tenant_id and actor_id, but do not include PII such as email or name. If PII is required for a legal request, it must be handled by the evidence service with elevated access control and separate export trails.

Examples: canonical event (ndjson line)
{
  "event_timestamp": "2025-02-10T18:22:33Z",
  "event_id": "0d9f3c2a-6a4c-4a1a-b3ff-9ef4c77d2b9f",
  "correlation_id": "6f2d7a8b-1c2e-4d3f-8a99-123456789abc",
  "actor_type": "service",
  "actor_id": "svc-kms-importer-01",
  "auth_method": "mTLS",
  "action": "key.import",
  "outcome": "success",
  "resource_type": "tenant-key",
  "resource_id": "key-72a4",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-834",
  "key_fingerprint": "sha256:3f9c1b...",
  "key_algorithm": "AES-256-GCM",
  "evidence_bundle_id": "eb-20250210-0001",
  "severity": "low"
}

SIEM alert example (pseudo)
- Rule: any event where action in [hsm-fallback, key.export-request, key-escrow] AND severity in [medium, high] -> create incident.
- Enrichment: attach evidence_bundle_id, tenant_id, actor_id, key_fingerprint, and link to archive path.

Operational runbook snippets
- If you receive an incident from SIEM for hsm-fallback: check HSM console, verify attestation logs, create evidence bundle (if not auto-created), notify on-call HSM team, escalate to platform SRE if fallback persists > 10 minutes.
- If SIEM flags possible unauthorized export: freeze the key (emit key.deactivate), generate emergency evidence bundle, initiate forensic snapshot, and notify legal/compliance.

Open questions and followups
- Decide canonical signing key rotation cadence for evidence service (TBD; currently proposal is quarterly).
- Determine final sampling defaults per tenant tier (free vs enterprise).
- Design detail: should evidence bundles be deduplicated across identical import operations? (tradeoff between storage and ease of lookup)

Appendix: helpful references and commands
- Evidence bundle verification: instructions for CLI verify-bundle --manifest manifest.json --sig proof.sig --cert attestation.pem
- Quick grep for event types in logs: grep 'action\":\"key.rotate\"' /var/log/kms/*.ndjson
- Contact list: @security-oncall, kms-ops-slack, evidence-service-owner@example.redwood.ai

End of playbook.
